title: Dietary sugars and body weight: systematic review and meta-analyses of randomised controlled trials and cohort studies
authors: Te Morenga L, Mallard S, Mann J
funder: The authors were supported by the University of Otago and the Riddet Institute, a New Zealand National Centre of Research Excellence. The research was supported by the University of Otago, Riddet Institute, and WHO. The authors undertook the submitted work for WHO for the purposes of updating WHO guidelines on sugars intake, and WHO provided some funding to the University of Otago towards the cost of carrying out the review.
authorConflicts: Support from the University of Otago, Riddet Institute and WHO; no other relevant financial relationships declared.
result: Adults on ad libitum diets: reduced intake of sugars, weight -0.80 kg (95% CI -1.21 to -0.39; 5 trials of 10 weeks to 8 months); increased intake, +0.75 kg (0.30 to 1.19; 10 trials). Isoenergetic exchange of sugars with other carbohydrates: 0.04 kg (-0.04 to 0.13). Children: trials of advice to reduce sugars had low compliance and showed no overall change; in cohort studies, odds ratio for overweight or obesity at about one year for the highest against the lowest intake of sugar-sweetened beverages 1.55 (1.32 to 1.82).
